confidence.reason: Photo outline (default): the visible container field is well measured (edges ~1 m, frame/scale confirmed, second tile set 0.2 m), but it is a lower bound (deeper toe to ~10 m invisible, detector-limited seaward edge, 24 faint patches excluded). Design outlines (Option 2 built 2018 but south reef/bridge only partly; 2004 design; 2011 relief zone) are placed to +-15 m and are envelopes. No post-renewal survey or as-built plan exists. Scale conflict resolved.
factors: + both arms resolve into individual 20 m containers on the 2020-08-08 Esri Wayback image (s3); s4 (2022 tile set) agrees to 0.2 m
+ position confirmed independently: the arms fall on the 4.0 / 4.5 m shoal contours of the Garmin Navionics SonarChart (within ~20 m)
+ arm length 134 m (N) vs the design drawing's 121 m to the -6 m contour (Jackson 2007 Fig 13 bar): within 10 %
- the visible field ends at about the -6 m contour; the deeper toe to -8 m is not visible, so the footprint is a lower bound
- channel containers (3, two faint) have an unresolved identity (the 2004 weir containers are N-S oriented and not visible in 2020)
- published envelope sizes (350 x 600, 450 x 250, 256 x 151 m) describe the design footprint or an asset envelope, not the container field
+ Corbett 2023 confirms Option 2 was built; the Option 2 -6 m envelope contains 97 % of the traced arms
+ Corbett Fig 2 and Jackson Fig 2 are the same CAD design on one scale (no scale conflict)

outline_versions.name: Renewed reef as seen on the 2020 aerial photo (visible container field, 8 Aug 2020)
outline_versions.method: Dark container patches thresholded on the 0.26 m/px Esri Wayback r9812 image (G<49), closed r=3.7 m, traced polygons; georeferenced from tile bounds; checked on the 2022 tile (0.2 m).
outline_versions.level: visible container field after the 2017-18 renewal (down to about the -6 m contour; the deeper toe is not visible, so this is a LOWER BOUND)
outline_versions.note: Default. Shows the reef as it actually is; the 3 'channel containers' and 2 wing patches are small and faint. 24 further faint patches (~660 m2) lie seaward/between the arms (faint_seaward_patches).

outline_versions.name: Renewal design Option 2 (2017, the layout the 2017-18 works followed), -6 m AHD envelope
outline_versions.method: Corbett et al. 2023 Fig 2 right, calibrated on its 50 m bar (0.5155 m/px), placed by the Jackson 2012 Fig 2/7 -> 2020 image chain (+-15 m, scale +-3 %); outer boundary of the nested contour group; crest loops = the black -2.5 m AHD contours (south loop closed by a 2-px hand patch).
outline_versions.level: -6 m AHD design contour envelope (outer limit of the design); crest -2.5 m AHD
outline_versions.note: A concept drawing: Corbett 2023 says the north reef was almost fully achieved, but the south reef and the bridge only partly. 97 % of the traced 2020 arms lie inside this envelope. No post-renewal as-built plan or survey exists.

outline_versions.name: 2004 revised design, -6 m AHD envelope (before the 2017-18 renewal)
outline_versions.method: Jackson et al. 2012 Fig 2 right (same CAD drawing as the contours on Fig 7), placed on the 2020 image by dark-patch NCC (corr 0.57) (+-15 m, scale +-10 %); outer boundary of the nested contours; crest loops = -2.5 m.
outline_versions.level: -6 m design contour envelope; crest -2.5 m AHD
outline_versions.note: Pre-renewal design; equals Corbett 2023 Option 1. 94.5 % of the traced arms lie inside.

outline_versions.name: Surveyed relief zone, bathymetric survey of 9 Jun 2011 (before the 2017-18 renewal)
outline_versions.method: Jackson et al. 2012 Fig 5a (Gold Coast City Council survey): zone of dense multi-colour contours (colour-pixel density in a 13 px window > 0.14, closed r=5), registered to the design drawing by chamfer fit and placed by the same chain (+-15 m). The figure has NO depth legend, so this is a relief zone, not a depth contour.

default_outline_decision: D7, Lior, 2026-10-10: default = the 2020-08-08 photo trace (visible container field); Option 2 design stays a toggle. Recorded in REQUESTS_FOR_LIOR.md (Decisions taken).
versions_info: Five outlines are stored. DEFAULT = the renewed reef as seen on the Esri aerial photo of 8 Aug 2020 (visible container field, 6,239 m2): no post-renewal survey or as-built drawing exists, so the photo is the only evidence of the state actually built. Renewal design Option 2 (Corbett et al. 2023 Fig 2, the layout the 2017-18 works followed, 13,941 m2 to the -6 m contour) is the design of the built version, but the south reef and bridge were only partly built. The 2004 revised design (13,631 m2) and the 2011 survey relief zone (4,922 m2, Jackson et al. 2012) describe the reef BEFORE the 84 containers of 2017-18. The Navionics 4.0 m shoals (537 m2) are indicative only. Design outlines are placed to +-15 m and are envelopes larger than the container field; the photo field is a lower bound (deeper toe invisible). Default outline = decision D7 by Lior, 2026-10-10 (keep the 2020 photo trace; Option 2 stays a toggle).

faint_seaward_patches.note: Faint dark patches not in the polygons (local-contrast detection on s3: G channel, blur 2 px, background gaussian sigma 30 px excluding traced polygons, diff > 4 DN, >= 10 m2, centroid y >= 241 m). Maybe buried containers or natural reef; not used in any outline. The first (cut-off) run found 20 patches / ~540 m2 with a slightly different recipe.
